summary.headline: TMPV Q1 FY27: India volumes up 46% to 182,000 units, but 4.5% commodity hit held India EBITDA at about 4%; JLR PBT fell to GBP 109 million.
summary.overview: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (formerly Tata Motors) posted Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 95,800 Cr, EBIT margin of 2.4% and PBT of Rs 1,600 Cr, down year on year. JLR wholesales fell about 10% (around 8,000 units) on Jaguar run-out, a supplier fire at Solihull and Middle East disruption, with JLR PBT at GBP 109 million versus GBP 351 million last year. India wholesales rose 46% to about 182,000 units and share rose 200 bps to 14.3%, but a 4.5% commodity hit in Q1 offset fixed-cost leverage and material savings, holding EBITDA margin at about 4%. Management says FY27 guidance for JLR is not changed.

segments.name: India PV (TMPV domestic)
segments.commentary: Wholesales about 182,000 units, up 46% YoY vs industry +24%; market share 14.3%, up 200 bps; firm #2 on registrations. EV volumes over 34,000 units (about 20% of sales), with July EV volume above 15,000 and EV share 43%.

segments.name: JLR
segments.commentary: Wholesales down about 10% YoY (about 8,000 units, around 3,000 below internal plan). Defender up YoY; Range Rover and Range Rover Sport hit by a chassis supplier fire early in the quarter. Retail down 14.5K YoY, with over 5,000 from Jaguar run-out and Middle East. China wholesales down 25%.

guidance_outlook: JLR FY27 guidance not changed; management says Q1 is not inconsistent with full-year guidance but needs strong rest-of-year performance.
TMPV targets higher double-digit volume growth in FY27 and 10% revenue growth per annum at group level.
Group targets $1.7 billion of cost savings across ex-works cost, warranty and fixed costs; detail promised with Q2 results.

India: Q2 commodity hit of about 3% expected; margins expected flattish vs Q1 after 0.5% July price increase, accelerated cost reduction (1.5% in Q1) and 1% IPL benefit; margin step-up expected in H2 as PLI accrues from Q3.
JLR expects about 12,000 EVs in FY27 (tentative); Type 01 and Range Rover GT impact mainly FY28.
India exports targeted at about 2x FY26 levels in FY27.
Avinya launch slips into 2027 due to platform change to JLR's Freelander platform.
capex_capacity: India Q1 capex Rs 1,300 Cr; to step up as next growth phase executes per Investor Day guidance.
JLR capitalisation rate 74%; spend over balance of year similar, shifting from engineering to capital as new facilities come online and four BEVs enter series production.
India monthly production about 63,000 in the latest month; target 65,000+ then near 70,000; Sanand lost five days to rainfall.
Sierra supply constrained by engine casting and sheet metal; improvement expected over next two months, major capacity addition from October.
India EV production ramped from about 9,000 a month to over 15,000 in the latest month; Punch.ev has 8-10 months waiting period.
JLR Range Rover Electric production start September; Range Rover Sport Electric and Range Rover GT later; Jaguar Type 01 production early next year.
demand_pricing: India volumes run-rate has consistently exceeded 60,000 a month vs earlier 45,000-50,000; EV mix 19% in Q1, 23% exit June, 24% in July.

India price increases total 1% (0.5% in April and 0.5% in July); commodity impact 4.5% in Q1 and about 3% expected in Q2; management says further calibrated increases and accelerated cost cuts will follow.
Dealer inventory about 30 days; management wants a significant build ahead of festive season and October retail.
EV bookings about 3.5x pre-Middle East crisis (Jan-Feb) levels; supply far below demand.
JLR China wholesales down 25%; management expects China to get worse before stabilising, citing retrospective taxes and luxury tax changes.
JLR VME (variable marketing expense) rose to 7.1%; JLR average transaction price trending up, targeting above GBP 80,000 per car in about 18 months.
JLR aluminium fell from about $3,500/t end-March to about $3,150/t end-June; some contracts reset quarterly, so Q2 may see extra raw material hit.
Industry PV volumes exceeded 1.3 million units, up 24% YoY; industry growth expected to moderate in H2 on higher base.

qa_highlights.question: Are JLR's Q1 temporary issues behind us and what is the volume recovery and Type 01 ramp plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jaguar wholesales of about 1,500 units lower QoQ are being run out over 3-6 months; Type 01 production starts early next year with impact in FY28, not FY27. The Solihull supplier fire is fully resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why only 1% price increase despite strong raw material headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is benchmarked against competitors to protect competitiveness; more frequent, progressive increases will follow as cost reductions allow, avoiding a steep single hike.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume and margin outlook for India?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting higher double-digit volume growth in FY27; margins to be neutralised through a mix of price increases and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Will JLR localise production in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Not localising existing models given volume scale; MoU with Stellantis for new US-specific vehicles (Defender brand), with a definitive agreement targeted by year end.

qa_highlights.question: How does rising EV mix affect JLR margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects BEV Range Rover models to be at least margin neutral and not discounted; the EMA cars replace low-margin models so should be neutral to accretive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sierra supply outlook for the festive season?
qa_highlights.answer: Engine casting and sheet-metal constraints are easing over the next two months, with major capacity additions from October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 margin outlook after the 3% commodity hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Net of price increase, cost reduction and the absence of Q1's 1% IPL seasonal impact, Q2 margins are expected to be flattish vs Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What JLR EV volume is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Tentatively about 12,000 EVs in FY27, starting with Range Rover Electric production in September.

risks_watch: JLR free cash flow deeply negative (about GBP 1 billion after working capital in Q1); working capital expected to reverse through the year.
China: retailer stress and new luxury taxes; management expects further deterioration before stabilising.
Commodity inflation: about 3% further hit in Q2 from quarterly contract resets; PLI certification for most models only from Q3-Q4.
Credit ratings: JLR at the edge of investment grade with negative watch; debt at GBP 3.6 billion.
Middle East disruption and Strait of Hormuz routing affecting retail and wholesale; Q1 MENA retail down about 1,400 units.
Supply constraints at Sierra and Punch.ev; India dealer stock at about 30 days.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India demand and EV momentum, but cautious on margins and JLR: management says Q1 was weaker than desired and China will get worse before it stabilises. Commitments are framed around actions (price, cost, PLI) rather than hard numbers.
key_quotes: So, we are setting a goal of 10% revenue growth per annum and focusing on the US market for a significant part of that.
So, the results was weaker than we would have liked, are not inconsistent with our full year guidance.
So, I would definitely be targeting higher double -digit growths in FY 27.
But it would be incorrect of me to stand here and say that I think all the bad news from China is all done yet.

growth.why: Management targets higher double-digit India PV volume growth and 10% group revenue growth p.a.; the Q1 India volume surge (+46%, 182k units, production ~63k/month rising to 65k-70k) and Sierra/EV capacity support it, but JLR is weak (PBT GBP 109m vs 351m), the JLR FY27 guidance is only held unchanged, and the $1.7bn cost plan detail is deferred to Q2.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India EBITDA was about 4% in Q1 and Q2 is guided flattish after a 3% commodity hit, with margin step-up in H2 as PLI accrues from Q3 (Rs 313 Cr accrued in Q1), while JLR EBIT margin is only 2.8% and commodity resets add pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 to Q2 FY27 (Range Rover Electric production from Sep
rows.why: Range Rover Electric production starts September and Sierra major capacity addition comes from October, with India production at about 63,000 a month targeting 65,000+ then near 70,000.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets higher double-digit India PV volume growth after a 46% Q1 rise to 182,000 units, EV volumes exceed 34,000, and exports are targeted near 2x FY26; JLR is weaker at about 10% wholesale decline with China down 25%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: India capex is set to step up from Rs 1,300 Cr in Q1 as the next growth phase executes per Investor Day guidance, and India run-rate has exceeded 60,000 a month against 45,000-50,000 earlier.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: JLR is weak with PBT down about 70% YoY, and management says the rest of the year needs strong performance just to hold guidance; the 1.7 bn cost plan detail is only due with Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: JLR PBT fell to GBP 109m from GBP 351m, wholesales were about 3,000 units below plan, and China is expected to worsen before stabilising, yet management held JLR FY27 guidance unchanged and says Q1 is not inconsistent with it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Range Rover Electric production starts September, Range Rover Sport Electric and GT follow later, and Jaguar Type 01 production starts early next year, though Avinya slips to 2027.

rows.label: EV bookings about 3.5x pre-Middle East crisis levels
rows.why: Bookings are about 3.5x Jan-Feb levels while EV production ramped from about 9,000 to over 15,000 a month and Punch.ev has an 8-10 month waiting period, so supply is the constraint.

rows.label: JLR cash burn and ratings pressure
rows.why: JLR free cash flow pre-working capital was GBP -352m and about GBP -1bn after working capital, with debt at GBP 3.6bn and JLR at the edge of investment grade on negative watch; management expects working capital to reverse through the year.

rows.label: Further calibrated India price increases
rows.why: India price increases total only 1% (0.5% April, 0.5% July) against a 4.5% Q1 commodity hit, and management says more frequent progressive increases will follow as cost cuts allow.

tone.note: Management was confident on India demand, share gains and EV momentum, and cautious on margins, JLR volumes and China, which it said will get worse before stabilising; analysts pushed on pricing, margins and the JLR recovery and Type 01 ramp.
